scope: Shared HTTP request cancellation, CDP target wall-clock budget, Windows launcher compatibility, bounded browser startup diagnostics and controlled nonresponding endpoint cleanup.

findings.finding: http.request timeout is socket inactivity. Math.min(500, remaining) does not bound the wall-clock lifetime of a response that continuously trickles bytes. The implementation guarantees an overall abort deadline, while the stated per-HTTP <=500ms contract is stronger.
findings.requiredResolution: Either provide a per-attempt absolute cancellation bound, or accurately define the supported contract as <=500ms idle timeout plus a global 15-second deadline.
findings.resolution: Contract explicitly specifies an HTTP idle budget of at most 500ms and a separate monotonic global 15-second wall-clock deadline with active cancellation. It makes no per-HTTP absolute-500ms guarantee. Trickle progress cannot extend the global budget.

findings.finding: The loop checks its monotonic deadline before awaiting HTTP but accepts a matching returned target without rechecking the deadline or abort state. A late callback processed before the abort timer may be accepted after budget exhaustion.
findings.requiredResolution: Recheck monotonic deadline and overall abort signal immediately after await and before accepting a target.
findings.resolution: Immediately after request resolves, waitForTarget checks both the overall abort signal and the monotonic deadline before examining or accepting a target. A controlled microtask test crosses the budget before the timer callback executes and confirms no late target is accepted.

findings.finding: The early launcher-exit path recognizes signalCode, while final diagnostics treat exitCode===null as alive even for a signaled process.
findings.requiredResolution: Use the same exitCode/signalCode liveness predicate in the final diagnostic.
findings.resolution: Final liveness checks exitCode===null together with absent signalCode. A signal-terminated launcher is reported as exited, including the observed signal.

coverageReview: The seventh request signal argument and fourth waitForTarget budget argument preserve existing six- and three-argument call forms. Existing request timeout semantics for other callers remain.
Response error settlement supports aborting incomplete response bodies without an unhandled response error. The global abort controller is cleared in finally after discovery completes.

Existing unit launcher fixture responds with HTTP200 empty list before the target. The added delayed-listen case covers launcher exit before the CDP endpoint exists and retains discovery within the real grace window.
BLOCK_CDP binds a separate owned nonresponding endpoint while the actual browser uses its own port. Final cleanup closes blocker connections and server after clipboard restoration.
Browser diagnostics are bounded to 8192 UTF-16 characters. Describing this as an exact 8KiB byte budget would be inaccurate.

Eight focused unit cases now include real never-headers and trickle HTTP, response-body abort settlement, delayed target/port publication, callback-vs-timer late-target rejection, response diagnostics and signal-terminated liveness. Unit mock changes are scoped to the individual test.

The overall timer is cleared in finally on success or failure. A pending request is actively destroyed through AbortSignal cancellation, allowing existing caller finally blocks to retain clipboard restoration ordering. Existing request callers with no signal keep their previous semantics.
